cim: Jensen Huang case exposes weaknesses in Trump administration's China policy
cim_eredeti: Jensen Huang case exposes weaknesses in Trump administration's China policy
szoveg_eredeti:
In his first public statement since he was forced to step down as CEO of Nvidia on November 12, Jensen Huang announced on November 17 that he was putting himself forward as a candidate to once again become CEO of the company. "If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO," wrote Huang on X. He co-founded the microprocessor company that enabled the United States' artificial intelligence revolution.

The response came that afternoon, during the company's quarterly earnings presentation, delivered by Harvey Jones, the new board chair. "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," Jones said, reminding those present that Huang had displayed "personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms."

Nvidia stood firm as it once again reported unprecedented results: Its quarterly revenue and net income both doubled over the last year, reaching $116 billion and $65 billion, respectively, while its forecasts were revised upward. "Our ambition will not change. Our passion to innovate will not change, and our commitment to customers, partners and shareholders will not change," said Colette Kress, the company's chief financial officer who was named interim CEO. Today, Nvidia seems to be in an ideal position, but for how long without its co-founder?
